linkedOutput.label: Economic output linked to Meta's advertising technologies
linkedOutput.definition: Meta's own estimate: 'Meta's advertising technologies are linked to $X billion in gross economic output annually.' Based on experimental research (Meta's 2024 US advertising revenue of $58 billion led to $215 billion in advertiser revenue across all states); total output for linked supply chains is estimated with BEA input-output tables. A modelled estimate of activity at advertisers and their supply chains, not Meta's own spending.

linkedJobs.label: Jobs linked to Meta's advertising technologies
linkedJobs.definition: Meta's own estimate of employment in advertisers' supply chains linked to its advertising technologies, from the same BEA input-output model. These are not Meta employees.

activeBusinesses.label: Businesses actively using Facebook
activeBusinesses.definition: Meta's estimate of businesses in the state that actively use Facebook; 'Active businesses are defined as those with a Facebook Page that has been logged into within the past month.'

longLivedAssets.label: Long-lived assets
longLivedAssets.definition: Long-lived assets by geographic area, which consist of property and equipment, net and operating lease right-of-use assets (FY2024 Form 10-K).

notes: usStates: one row per state from Meta's own 'Meta in <State>' fact sheets (research.facebook.com/economiccontribution, 50 states; no DC sheet), each read in full. Output and jobs are Meta's modelled estimates of activity at advertisers and their supply chains linked to Meta ads (BEA input-output multipliers), not Meta payroll or spending; the national sheet gives $547.6 billion and 3,400,000 jobs. research.facebook.com refuses scripted requests, so the 50 PDFs were opened in a real browser (each redirects to a signed fbcdn.net copy, downloaded and read); source.url is the stable research.facebook.com/file/... address, which the automated quote checker cannot fetch. Sites: corporate HQ from the 10-K (which says Meta owns 27 data center locations), plus data centers from datacenters.atmeta.com (page read Nov 2026, undated, and it lists sites announced after FY2024). Selection rule: every data center outside North America, and the seven U.S. data centers with the largest stated investment, limited to sites that broke ground in 2024 or earlier; newer announced sites (Lebanon IN, El Paso TX, Bowling Green OH, Beaver Dam WI, Tulsa OK, Sturgeon County AB) are left out. Several states host more than one data center (AL, IN, OH, TX), so data-center figures are not summed into states. Long-lived assets: the 10-K discloses only the U.S. and the rest of the world. Revenue by geography is in the records and not repeated.
